name: ADS7830 8-channel 8-bit I2C ADC
description: Texas Instruments 8-bit, 8-channel analog-to-digital converter with an I2C interface: one command byte starts a conversion and one byte comes back (code = Vin × 256 / VREF). Up to 70 kSPS; 4 addresses (0x48–0x4B). Sold as: Adafruit ADS7830 8-Channel 8-Bit ADC with I2C (#5836), 16 pins on two headers (VIN, GND, SCL, SDA, REF, COM, AD0, AD1 / A7–A0), REF tied to VIN, I2C address 0x48.
eli5: Gives your board eight extra analog inputs, so it can read lots of knobs and sensors that output a voltage.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply 3–5 V; also the ADC reference (REF is tied to VIN on the board). Use the same voltage as your microcontroller's logic.

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10 kΩ pull-up to VIN on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10 kΩ pull-up to VIN on the board)

pins.name: REF
pins.description: ADC reference (REFIN/REFOUT); tied to VIN through the Ext Ref jumper. Leave unconnected.

pins.name: COM
pins.description: Common (negative) input for single-ended channels; tied to GND through the Ext Com jumper. Leave unconnected.

pins.name: AD0
pins.description: Address bit 0 (10 kΩ pull-down): low = 0x48, high (to VIN) adds 1

pins.name: AD1
pins.description: Address bit 1 (10 kΩ pull-down): high (to VIN) adds 2

pins.name: A7
pins.description: Analog input channel 7, 0 V to VREF (= VIN); never above VIN + 0.2 V

pins.name: A6
pins.description: Analog input channel 6, 0 V to VREF (= VIN); never above VIN + 0.2 V

pins.name: A5
pins.description: Analog input channel 5, 0 V to VREF (= VIN); never above VIN + 0.2 V

pins.name: A4
pins.description: Analog input channel 4, 0 V to VREF (= VIN); never above VIN + 0.2 V

pins.name: A3
pins.description: Analog input channel 3, 0 V to VREF (= VIN); never above VIN + 0.2 V

pins.name: A2
pins.description: Analog input channel 2, 0 V to VREF (= VIN); never above VIN + 0.2 V

pins.name: A1
pins.description: Analog input channel 1, 0 V to VREF (= VIN); never above VIN + 0.2 V

pins.name: A0
pins.description: Analog input channel 0, 0 V to VREF (= VIN); never above VIN + 0.2 V

buildNotes: Each reading: write one command byte (SD C2 C1 C0 PD1 PD0 x x), then read one byte. Single-ended channel order in C2..C0 is not binary: CH0=000, CH1=100, CH2=001, CH3=101, CH4=010, CH5=110, CH6=011, CH7=111 (e.g. 0x84 = CH0, 0xC4 = CH1).
On this board REF is tied to VIN, so keep PD1 = 0 (internal 2.5 V reference off; PD bits 01 = ADC on). Volts = code × VIN / 256: about 12.9 mV per step at 3.3 V.
Power VIN from the same voltage as your microcontroller (3.3 V for ESP32 / Pico): the board's 10 kΩ SDA/SCL pull-ups go to VIN.
Inputs read 0 V to VIN; never drive an input above VIN + 0.2 V or below −0.2 V.
AD0/AD1 are pulled low (0x48); tie AD0 to VIN for 0x49, AD1 for 0x4A, both for 0x4B. This board has more than 8 pins, so wire it with jumper leads.

driver.code:
# ADS7830 8-channel 8-bit I2C ADC (Texas Instruments), MicroPython driver.
# From the TI datasheet SBAS302C: write one command byte
#   SD C2 C1 C0 PD1 PD0 X X
# which starts a conversion, then read one byte (straight binary, D7 = MSB).
# Code = Vin * 256 / VREF, so Vin = code * VREF / 256 (1 LSB = VREF / 256).
#
# On the Adafruit breakout (#5836) the REF pin is tied to VIN, so VREF = the supply
# voltage and the internal 2.5 V reference must stay OFF (PD1 = 0, datasheet:
# "If using an external reference, PD1 must be set to '0'"). Pass internal_ref=True
# only if you cut the board's Ext Ref jumper and want the internal 2.5 V reference.
import time

# Single-ended channel select bits C2 C1 C0 for CH0..CH7 (datasheet Table 2, SD = 1)
_SINGLE = (0b000, 0b100, 0b001, 0b101, 0b010, 0b110, 0b011, 0b111)
# Differential pairs (SD = 0): index = (positive, negative) pair, Table 2
_DIFF = {(0, 1): 0b000, (2, 3): 0b001, (4, 5): 0b010, (6, 7): 0b011,
         (1, 0): 0b100, (3, 2): 0b101, (5, 4): 0b110, (7, 6): 0b111}


class ADS7830:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x48, vref=3.3, internal_ref=False):
        """vref: the voltage on the REF pin (the board's VIN by default)."""
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        self.internal_ref = internal_ref
        self.vref = 2.5 if internal_ref else vref
        # PD1 PD0: 01 = internal reference OFF, A/D converter ON (external REF)
        #          11 = internal reference ON,  A/D converter ON
        self._pd = 0b11 if internal_ref else 0b01
        if internal_ref:
            # The internal reference turns on after the first command with PD1 = 1
            # and a STOP; it needs settling time before 8-bit accurate results
            # (datasheet Figure 12: tens of ms without a REF capacitor, longer with one).
            self._convert(0x80 | (self._pd << 2))
            time.sleep_ms(50)

    def _convert(self, cmd):
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([cmd]))
        return self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, 1)[0]

    def read_raw(self, channel):
        """Single-ended conversion of channel 0-7 against COM; returns 0-255."""
        if not 0 <= channel <= 7:
            raise ValueError('channel must be 0-7')
        cmd = 0x80 | (_SINGLE[channel] << 4) | (self._pd << 2)
        return self._convert(cmd)

    def read_diff_raw(self, pos, neg):
        """Differential conversion (pos - neg) of an adjacent pair, e.g. (0, 1); 0-255."""
        c = _DIFF.get((pos, neg))
        if c is None:
            raise ValueError('pair must be CH0/CH1, CH2/CH3, CH4/CH5 or CH6/CH7')
        return self._convert((c << 4) | (self._pd << 2))

    def read_voltage(self, channel):
        """Channel voltage in volts: code * VREF / 256."""
        return self.read_raw(channel) * self.vref / 256

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from ads7830 import ADS7830

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
adc = ADS7830(i2c, vref=3.3)  # board powered from 3.3 V: REF = VIN = 3.3 V
while True:
    r0 = adc.read_raw(0)
    r3 = adc.read_raw(3)
    print('A0=%d %.2fV A3=%d %.2fV' % (r0, r0 * 3.3 / 256, r3, r3 * 3.3 / 256))
    time.sleep(1)
